title: Middle-tier server threat ledger 2023-01..2026-10 (ranked)
summary: Ranking by likelihood x impact over ~516 primary advisories + CISA KEV: (1) H2/H3/QUIC protocol-state resource exhaustion; (2) path/host canonicalization and fail-open authz logic (dominates KEV); (3) request smuggling/parser differentials; (4) memory corruption in C/C++ servers (RCE tail); (5) agent/MCP-layer authz and origin-binding gaps; (6) TLS validation logic incl. PQC downgrade.
specifics: Raw TSV/JSON in state/raw/round-001/01-data/; detailed notes in 01-...progress.md
overclaim_risk: Memory/logic split via keyword heuristic (+-5pp); advisories != exploits; 2026 counts inflated by AI-discovery wave and GHSA backfill.
underclaim_risk: CDN/proprietary desyncs rarely get CVEs; silent fixes uncounted.

verify.note: Ranking is judgement; GHSA-publishing projects (Envoy/Caddy/undici) over-counted vs nginx/httpd; "dominates KEV" holds for gateway/appliance products, not OSS servers (<=5 OSS KEV entries).

title: Share of middle-tier vulns memory safety would NOT prevent
summary: C/C++ servers: ~61% of 236 advisories are logic/resource (nginx 8/35=23%, httpd 48/77=62%, Envoy ~60/84). Memory-safe servers (Tomcat, Go, undici, Caddy, Pingora, quinn, quiche, hyper/h2, Node HTTP; ~280 advisories) <=1% memory corruption. KEV 2023-26: 100% of 5 OSS middle-tier entries non-memory; 80.3% of all KEV adds (715/890) and 80.5% of edge-gateway adds (99/123) non-memory.
overclaim_risk: Rust memory bugs become panics (DoS), not zero impact.
underclaim_risk: Memory safety removes the RCE tail (e.g. CVE-2026-42533 CVSS4 9.2, CVE-2026-23918).

verify.note: Verifier recomputed KEV non-memory 81.2% (723/890) vs claimed 80.3%; CWE-list dependent; nginx 2026 alone is ~19/26 memory, so the 23% nginx logic share is a multi-year average.

title: HTTP/2, HTTP/3, QUIC protocol-state resource exhaustion
summary: Recurring lineage 2023-2026; Rapid Reset was a record ITW DDoS (Google 398M rps) and is in KEV. Variants each year; Rust Pingora and quinn affected. Implementations that bound concurrent handlers (not just open streams) were unaffected by MadeYouReset per CERT vendor statements.

verify.note: HTTP/2 Bomb CVE-2026-49975 (Calif/Codex, 2026-06-02) is a protocol-composition bug (HPACK amplification + zero window) that hit nginx, httpd, IIS, Envoy, Pingora in default config (>880k hosts); Varnish VSV00017 shows MadeYouReset bypassed the Rapid Reset limit.

title: Structural controls implied by the ledger (for THREAT_MODEL / SPEC_INVARIANTS)
summary: Invariants: (I1) per-connection and per-tenant memory/CPU budgets covering decoded headers, HPACK/QPACK tables, reassembly buffers and decompressed bytes; bound concurrent handlers, not open streams. (I2) single canonical request representation computed once; routing and authz consume only it; reject ambiguous framing (TE+CL, bodies on GET/HEAD, obs-fold). (I3) non-H1 or strictly regenerated upstream framing. (I4) fail-closed config load: any missing security material aborts startup. (I5) no panics reachable from network input (panic=DoS). (I6) agent endpoints: Host/Origin allowlist on by default, session bound to principal, token audience = this resource. (I7) hours-scale patch pipeline and runtime feature kill-switches (H2/H3/compression). Gates: differential fuzz vs hyper/nginx; regression corpus seeded from every CVE above.

verify.note: Design inference, hypotheses for next stage.

title: Escapes cluster in glue, not in the core isolation primitive
summary: Across 2022-2026 advisories for Wasmtime, WAMR, Wasmer, Firecracker, Cloud Hypervisor, Kata, Deno and KVM, sandbox breaks fall into five groups: (a) JIT or codegen miscompiles; (b) host filesystem path handling (symlinks, trailing slashes, TRUNCATE); (c) component-model or hostcall ABI glue; (d) virtio device emulation in VMMs; (e) orchestration and policy layers (Kata annotations). Hardware virtualization and the Wasm bounds model are rarely the failure point themselves. The glue around them is.
specifics: Wasmtime 2026: 57 advisories. About 3 are fs-sandbox escapes, 5 critical are codegen or ABI bugs, and about 15 are guest-triggered host panics. Kata 2026: at least 6 critical or high guest-to-host bugs via virtiofs, annotations and Dragonball virtio. Cloud Hypervisor: CVE-2026-45782 (UAF in virtio-blk). Firecracker: CVE-2026-5747 (virtio-pci OOB write).
overclaim_risk: This classification is my own (E-level synthesis over B-level data). Counts depend on each project's disclosure policy: gVisor publishes no GHSA, so it can look cleaner than it is.
underclaim_risk: Someone could read 'the core primitive is sound' as 'Wasm or VMs are fine'. In practice the glue ships with the primitive and cannot be avoided.

title: LOCAL measurement: Wasmtime 36.0.19 instantiation, density and teardown (i9-14900HX, Linux 6.17)

title: Fuel vs epoch: epoch is about 2x cheaper, and fuel accounting has had bypasses
summary: Wasmtime PR #3699 (2022-01-19): epoch interruption is about twice as fast as fuel on control-flow-heavy code such as SpiderMonkey.wasm, but it is non-deterministic. 2026 advisories show fuel can be circumvented or amplified (CVE-2026-115390 exponential via call_ref/catch; CVE-2026-115380 WASIp0 poll_oneoff; CVE-2026-115389 hostcall lifting beyond the fuel limit). A local measurement interrupted an infinite loop about 1.2 ms after the epoch tick.
specifics: Recommended setup: epoch ticks at 1-10 ms from a timer thread, a per-request deadline in ticks, plus a wall-clock watchdog, plus a ResourceLimiter. Use fuel only when deterministic replay is needed, never as the DoS bound.

title: What survives a panic, trap, OOM or infinite loop (measured)
summary: Local tests on Wasmtime 36.0.19. (1) A host-function panic during a guest call is caught via catch_unwind inside Wasmtime and re-raised to the embedder; the embedder can catch it with catch_unwind if panic=unwind. Panics inside non-catching libcalls abort the process (traphandlers.rs). (2) A guest OOB access gives Trap::MemoryOutOfBounds, and the same instance stays callable afterwards, so its state may be inconsistent: discard the store. (3) memory.grow past the ResourceLimiter returns -1. (4) An infinite loop ends with Trap::Interrupt via epoch. Teardown with pooling: 4.4 us per store (madvise reset). For native fork-per-request: fork+exit+wait takes 124 us p50 from a small parent but 33 ms from a parent with 1 GiB resident, so prefork must fork from a small zygote.
specifics: Code: 04-bench/src/bin/forkpanic.rs, run2.txt. About 15 of the 2026 Wasmtime advisories are 'guest can panic host'. With panic=abort, each one becomes a whole-server DoS.
overclaim_risk: The test used a single store and module. Async and fiber paths were not tested.
underclaim_risk: Per-request Store plus catch_unwind gives PHP-like 'request dies, server lives' semantics at about 7 us.

verify.note: run2 output confirms; single run.

title: Safe Rust is not a security boundary against adversarial code
summary: On 2026-10-24, rust-lang/rust has 166 open issues labeled I-unsound. #25860 (implied bounds plus variance) has been open since 2015-05-28. The cve-rs crate (5.4k stars) demonstrates memory corruption in 100% safe Rust. Capability-typed APIs in native Rust are therefore sound against buggy but benign code and unsound against malicious or prompt-injected code.

title: Process self-sandboxing: seccomp-bpf plus Landlock ABI 1-11

Gaps: chdir, stat, chmod, chown and fcntl are not restrictable, and rulesets nest at most 16 layers. This is the backstop layer for both the native and the Wasm designs. It does not stop cross-tenant attacks inside one process.
specifics: Use the highest available ABI with best-effort fallback. Use seccomp allowlists generated from strace of the integration tests.

title: Spectre and side-channel posture per substrate
summary: Wasmtime: call_indirect and br_table masked; dynamic memories get bounds-check masking; aarch64 csdb off by default; guard-page (static) memories rely on page faults. Swivel (USENIX Sec 2021) showed in-process Wasm cannot fully stop cross-tenant Spectre; separate processes block it except for cross-process branch-predictor poisoning. V8 and Cloudflare rely on timer freezing, no SharedArrayBuffer or threads, and process isolation on anomaly. VMs: the hypervisor plus CPU microcode, but SMT siblings must not be shared across tenants (Nanvix notes the same). Conclusion: secret-bearing tenants of different principals should not share a process. Use cordons, one process per tenant group, and SMT-aware core pinning.
overclaim_risk: No 2024-2026 public cross-tenant Spectre exploit against Wasmtime serverless was found.
underclaim_risk: The absence of a public exploit is not safety. Transient-execution attacks keep appearing.

verify.note: No source re-fetched; post-2021 variants (Retbleed/Inception/BHI) not covered.

title: Decision table: isolation substrate keyed by code provenance and threat model
summary: (P1) First-party code in the server's repo, human- or agent-written but passing verifiers; threat is bugs, not malice. Run native Rust handlers in-process under capability-typed contexts with #![forbid(unsafe_code)], clippy disallowed std::fs/net/process, panic=unwind, catch_unwind plus a per-request arena or Store at the request boundary, a whole-server seccomp+Landlock policy, and a supervisor restart. Wasm adds 7-23 us per request plus ABI cost and a large glue CVE surface without removing the dominant bug class (logic and authz). (P2) Semi-trusted: agent-generated plugins or handlers not human-reviewed, or code exposed to prompt injection. Run Wasmtime components in-process with the hardening config from wasmtime-memory64-spectre-config, no WASI fs preopens, host-mediated capabilities with I/O budgets, a fresh Store per request discarded on any trap, all inside the seccomp/Landlock'd worker process. (P3) Third-party, multi-tenant, mutually distrusting: Wasm or isolates inside per-cordon worker processes (grouped by trust tier) with namespaces, seccomp and Landlock, no shared memory or threads, coarse timers, a patch SLO under 72 h. Never Wasm-only. For high-value tenants, one microVM per tenant (Firecracker snapshot about 69 ms, Hyperlight about 8 ms) with nested virt disabled and /dev/kvm restricted. (P4) Arbitrary native or agent tool execution (shell, Python, npm): microVM (Firecracker or Cloud Hypervisor from snapshot) or gVisor. Never Wasm or in-process.
specifics: Reversal conditions: (a) if Wasmtime goes 12 months with no critical escape on the x86_64 tier-1 config and VeriISLE x64 coverage exceeds 80% of lowering rules, P3 can drop the per-cordon process split for low-value tenants; (b) if Hyperlight 1.0 ships with under 2 ms cold start and an independent audit, it replaces Wasm-in-process for P2; (c) if server-class CHERI ships, revisit P1/P2 in-process compartments.
overclaim_risk: This is a synthesis (grade E) built on B/A nodes. The numbers are from heterogeneous hardware.
underclaim_risk: Over-isolating first-party code costs density and DX for little security gain. The operator's 'PHP miracle' comes mostly from per-request state discard, not from a VM boundary.

title: Verdict: Wasm is the right boundary for untrusted or semi-trusted code, not for first-party code; it is never sufficient alone for third-party code
summary: Evidence: (1) Wasm escapes recur at about 5 criticals a year in 2026 under LLM auditing, and the glue (WASI fs, component ABI) is the main surface. (2) Safe-Rust capabilities are not adversarially sound (166 I-unsound issues). (3) Per-request Wasm costs 7 us p50 pooled and about 7 KiB minimum RSS (local), so density is excellent. title: Sketch: PQ-ready attenuable capability token (two-tier: HMAC chain locally, ML-DSA only at trust-domain crossings)
summary: Tier L (issuer = verifier, the dominant middle-tier case): macaroon-style chained MAC (HMAC-SHA256 or KMAC256, 256-bit root key from HKDF over a KMS secret) with typed caveats. That costs 32 B per caveat, is PQ-safe today, and needs no signature. Tier X (cross-domain delegation or third-party verification): the root block is signed with a hybrid Ed25519+ML-DSA-44 composite (or ML-DSA-65 for CNSA 2.0 alignment), and further attenuation within the domain stays MAC-based via the holder's discharge. Per-block public-key attenuation (Biscuit-style) is allowed but costs about 3.7-5.3 KB per hop.
specifics: Size arithmetic, signature material only, per public-key block (next_pk + sig): Ed25519 96 B; ML-DSA-44 3,732 B; ML-DSA-65 5,261 B; ML-DSA-87 7,219 B; hybrid Ed25519+ML-DSA-44 3,828 B; SLH-DSA-128s 7,888 B. Three-hop chain (root + 2 attenuations): Ed25519 288 B; ML-DSA-44 11.2 KB; ML-DSA-65 15.8 KB (21.0 KB with base64url); SLH-DSA-128s 23.7 KB. Two-tier design, 1 ML-DSA-65 root + 5 MAC caveats: about 5.3 KB + 160 B. Wire rules: carry Tier X tokens in the body or a dedicated header with an explicit max (16 KB); allow a by-reference handle (token hash) after the first presentation (session-bound cache), to avoid per-request multi-KB headers. Algorithm agility: a per-block alg id from a closed enum {ed25519, mldsa44, mldsa65, hybrid-ed25519-mldsa44, hmac-sha256}. Unknown alg means reject. No 'none'.
overclaim_risk: Header-limit concerns depend on proxy defaults (nginx and Node header limits not re-fetched this round).
underclaim_risk: Choosing per-hop PQ signatures by default would multiply token size about 39x vs Ed25519 (11.2 KB vs 288 B for 3 hops) for a property (public verifiability) most middle-tier deployments do not need.

title: Invariant: No ambient authority (statement for Lean model + Rust type boundary)
summary: For every trace t of the server and every effect e in t (DB query, outbound HTTP, file op, tool call, state write) performed while serving request r: there exists c in Held(r, t, before e) with permits(c, e). Held(r) changes only by (i) Grant: at request entry, Held := derive(verified_token(r)) union route_endowment(route(r)), where route_endowment is static config; (ii) Introduction: c passed as an explicit argument by a holder; (iii) Creation: capabilities to freshly allocated objects. No effect API is callable without a Cap argument, and Cap has no public constructor.
specifics: Lean: `theorem no_ambient : ∀ t r e, e ∈ effects t r → ∃ c ∈ held t r (pre e), permits c e`. `held` is defined inductively by the 3 rules above, so the theorem reduces to an induction over the step relation. Rust: `pub struct Cap<O: Op>(PhantomData<O>, Sealed)` with a crate-private constructor; effect fns take `&Cap<O>`; `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in handler crates; a CI gate denies std::fs/std::net/tokio::net imports in handler crates (cargo-deny, clippy disallowed-methods). Verus: a spec fn `derive(token) -> Set<Perm>` with an ensures clause that derive is a subset of the token's authorized set.
overclaim_risk: A type boundary does not hold under unsafe, FFI or a compromised dependency. The TCB includes rustc and the effect-API crate.
underclaim_risk: Type-level ocap discipline is checkable today at zero proof cost for the handler code.

title: Invariant: Attenuation monotonicity
summary: Denotation [[t]] is a subset of Requests × Time. For every token t and every block or caveat b, [[append(t, b)]] ⊆ [[t]]. For policy updates p -> p' accepted without human approval: [[p']] ⊆ [[p]] (SMT-checked as `implies(p', p)`). For delegation chains: [[t_k]] ⊆ [[t_{k-1}]] ⊆ ... ⊆ [[t_0]] ⊆ ceiling(issuer).
specifics: Lean: define `denote : Token → Request → Prop` with denote (append t b) r := denote t r ∧ caveat b r, so monotonicity is a one-line ∧-elimination proof. The burden moves to proving that the Rust checker refines `denote` (DRT plus Verus). Biscuit-style Datalog blocks need an extra side condition: facts from block i are not visible to authority checks unless explicitly trusted (scope), else a later block could add facts that satisfy an earlier check. Prove `scope_isolation`. Use cedar-policy-symcc checkImplies (SymCC soundness is proved in Lean) to gate policy diffs in CI.
overclaim_risk: Monotonicity of the set does not prevent confused deputy if the deputy merges authority from several tokens.
underclaim_risk: It is trivially provable once caveats are conjunctive. Do not design caveats that can widen, such as disjunctive blocks.

title: Invariant: Confused-deputy freedom as integrity noninterference on authority selection
summary: Deputy D serving request r may exercise only authority in A(r) = [[token(r)]] ∪ Endow(route(r)). Noninterference form: let inputs split into high-integrity H (verified token, route, static config, trusted user query) and low-integrity L (request body fields not bound by the token, fetched documents, tool and LLM outputs). For all executions σ1, σ2 with σ1|H = σ2|H: AuthSel(σ1) = AuthSel(σ2), where AuthSel is the sequence of (capability id, op kind, target designation source) exercised. L may affect data arguments only through label-checked sinks: label(arg) ⊑ sink_policy(op).
specifics: Concretely the server must (1) designate targets by capability, not by name strings taken from L (the 'Authority Is Not a String' rule); (2) never merge the deputy's own authority with the requester's for one effect unless the effect is in A(r); (3) propagate integrity labels across MCP and A2A hops (fixes the CaMeL non-composition). Lean: a 2-run relational property over a small-step semantics of the handler DSL (as in Devriese et al. logical relations). Verus: a ghost label on values, and a requires clause on effect APIs that the target designation is high-integrity. Test oracle: a hyperproperty fuzz. Run each request twice with L randomized, assert equal AuthSel traces (DST harness).
overclaim_risk: NI for general handler code is undecidable to check fully. We prove it for the mediator and DSL, then test it (2-run fuzz) for handler code.
underclaim_risk: The 2-run fuzz is cheap and catches most real confused-deputy bugs (argument-designated targets).

title: Invariant: Deterministic, total, fail-closed authorization decision
summary: authorize(req, ents, pols) is a total function independent of wall-clock, scheduling and allocator state. Resource bounds are fuel (step counts), not time: exhaustion means Deny with reason ResourceExhausted, reproducibly. Any error in a forbid policy, or in token verification, means Deny.
specifics: Rejects Biscuit-default max_time=1ms semantics. CI gates: (1) cedar-policy-symcc verifyNeverErrors on every forbid policy; (2) a DRT target comparing our wrapper decision with the Lean spec under an error-to-deny overlay; (3) a determinism test that runs each fuzz case under a CPU-stress cgroup and asserts identical decisions; (4) parser fuzz with -rss_limit_mb=512 and -max_len=65536 on policy, schema and token parsers (motivated by GHSA-m84h-6f26-p3p7); (5) never parse untrusted policy text on the request path. Policies are loaded and validated at deploy time only.

FN-DSA final plus a FIPS module, then switch Tier X to FN-DSA-512.

title: PQ size/MTU reality: hybrid KEM +~1.2 KB each way; ML-DSA chain +~14.7 KB; tldr.fail split-ClientHello breakage; QUIC 3x amplification forces extra RTT
summary: X25519MLKEM768 client share 1216 B (32+1184), server share 1120 B (32+1088) -> ClientHello exceeds one TCP segment/QUIC Initial. tldr.fail documented servers/middleboxes that did a single read() and reset: Vercel (fixed 2023-08-23), Zscaler (2023-09-28), Palo Alto (2025-03-27), Broadcom ProxySG 7.3.22.1, Apache Traffic Server (2025-06-25), Envoy (config), ingress-nginx passthrough, Cisco (unknown). Chrome measured ~4% handshake slowdown from hybrid KEM bytes. Cloudflare: ML-DSA-44 WebPKI handshake adds ~14.7 kB (2x1312 B pk + 5x2420 B sigs incl. 2 SCTs); SLH-DSA ~39 kB; CF 2021 experiment: >10 kB extra -> steep client/middlebox failure increase, <9 kB -> ~15% slower. QUIC: RFC 9000 3x anti-amplification; CoNEXT'22: 35% of classical cert chains already exceed it, 38% of handshakes need >1 RTT; an ML-DSA chain (~15-18 kB) cannot fit a ~3.6-7.5 kB budget -> guaranteed extra RTT(s) unless MTC (proof <=800 B) or cert compression.
specifics: L5 acceptance tests: (1) TLS listener must accept a ClientHello delivered 1 byte per read (fragmented-ClientHello fuzz case); (2) QUIC listener: measure handshake RTTs with 1200-B and 1350-B client Initials and a ML-DSA-65 private-PKI chain; budget <=2 RTT with RFC 8879 compression on; (3) PQ-auth path not offered on public listener until MTC.
overclaim_risk: Derived QUIC budget numbers (E) combine B-grade inputs.
underclaim_risk: KEM-only PQ is cheap (~4%); size problem is authentication, not key agreement.

title: HTTP/1.1 desync is alive: 0.CL / Expect-based / chunk-terminator classes (2025) => use HTTP/2 (or h2c) upstream
summary: Kettle 'HTTP/1.1 must die' (2025-08-06, upd 2025-10-17): new 0.CL, double-desync, Expect-based desync; Akamai CVE-2025-32094 (74 bounties, $221k), Cloudflare internal H2 desync (~24M sites), total >$350k. Thesis: upstream HTTP/1.1 is inherently ambiguous; HTTP/2+ upstream removes the class; H2->H1 downgrade adds a 4th length interpretation. Chunk line-terminator family: Go CVE-2025-22871 (bare LF, fixed 1.23.8/1.24.2), Python h11 CVE-2025-43859 (CVSS 9.1). hyper rejects bare LF in chunk lines (code read 2026-10-13).
specifics: L5 invariant (parser canonicality): for every byte stream S accepted by our h1 parser, re-serializing parse(S) and re-parsing yields identical message boundaries; reject: CL+TE together, duplicate CL with differing values, TE other than exactly 'chunked', bare LF/CR anywhere in framing, obs-fold, Expect on bodyless methods, body on GET/HEAD/OPTIONS (configurable). Upstream: speak HTTP/2 (h2c or TLS) to backends by default; if HTTP/1.1 upstream, regenerate framing (never forward client CL/TE verbatim). Differential fuzz vs nginx/HAProxy/hyper with HTTP Request Smuggler v3 probes.
overclaim_risk: Bounty totals describe deployments, not parser libraries.
underclaim_risk: Strict Rust parser alone is not enough: desync is a two-parser property — the fix is architectural (normalize + H2 upstream).

title: Dependency update cooldown (no native Cargo support)
summary: Neither Cargo nor crates.io has a native minimum-release-age as of 2026-10-24 (searched CHANGELOG/unstable.md). Evidence for: arrayref malicious versions lived 86-107 min; tokio 1.54.0 was yanked ~2 days after release (RUSTSEC-2026-0384/CVE-2026-115567; 1.54.1 on 2026-10-21 = what my lock resolved). underclaim_risk: Costs almost nothing for a solo dev with --locked.
specifics: dependabot.yml: package-ecosystem: cargo, cooldown: {default-days: 7, semver-patch-days: 3}, security PRs bypass automatically; human merge only; CI `cargo vet`. title: Reproducible Rust build: measured dir-independence, remap flags, and open gaps
summary: Own experiment (rustc 1.88.0, same host/user): hyper1+tokio+rustls0.23(aws-lc-rs, C via cc) release build with lto=true, codegen-units=1, debug=1, --locked --offline. Same source built from two directories: naive builds differ (sha256 2b5f06cf.. vs 6f74c474..); with RUSTFLAGS="--remap-path-prefix=<srcdir>=/src --remap-path-prefix=$HOME/.cargo/registry/src=/cargo/registry --remap-path-prefix=$HOME/.rustup=/rustup" the two builds are byte-identical (bb7b60e4..) even WITHOUT -Wl,--build-id=none; CARGO_TARGET_DIR location does not matter (same hash as naive original). ~33-42 s/build. Untested: different toolchain host, glibc/linker versions, CARGO_HOME, cross-machine, proc-macro/build.rs time stamps. Context: RELEASES.md lists a stabilization item for --remap-path-prefix under 1.97.0 (2026-07-09) and --remap-path-scope under 1.95.0 (2026-04-16); cargo -Ztrim-paths still unstable (no mention in Cargo CHANGELOG). Known amplifiers: codegen-units=16 + LTO, rustdoc nondeterminism with varying path lengths (Yocto), debuginfo embedding paths (reproducible-builds list 2024-08). NixOS minimal ISO: 1434/1501 (95.54%) paths reproducible in 2021 claim; full independent rebuild of 25.11 ISO by Engelen Dec 2025 but r13y checks still use binary cache.
overclaim_risk: Single host/toolchain; identical hash on one machine is necessary but not sufficient for independent-rebuilder reproducibility.
underclaim_risk: Dir-independence is the most common practical break and is solved with three remap flags; cost is near zero.
specifics: CI stage: build twice in distinct dirs (/build/a and /build/b) in a pinned container (digest-pinned image, rust-toolchain.toml channel=1.99.1), with RUSTFLAGS as above, `-C codegen-units=1 -C lto=fat`, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git log -1 --format=%ct), `--locked`, `cargo vendor`+offline; pass: sha256(a)==sha256(b). Weekly: second independent rebuilder (different cloud/runner OS image) must match the published hash (store hash in attestation). Never ship from the same runner that attests without the double build.

title: SLSA v1.2 Build L3 via GitHub reusable workflow + actions/attest@v4; crates.io trusted publishing
summary: SLSA v1.2 Build track (status Approved): L1 provenance exists; L2 adds authentic + hosted; L3 adds unforgeable (signing key inaccessible to user build steps) + isolated (ephemeral, no platform secrets, no cache poisoning). GitHub guidance: L3 needs signing in a reusable workflow separate from the build job. actions/attest@v4 requires id-token:write, contents:read, attestations:write; verify with `gh attestation verify BIN -R org/repo`. crates.io trusted publishing (RFC 3691, July 2025) uses OIDC via rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action@v1; Jan 2026 added GitLab CI and an option to disable token publishing so only Trusted Publishing can publish. TigerBeetle release.yml precedent: top-level `permissions: {}`, a protected `release` environment, actions pinned by full commit SHA, OIDC for npm.
overclaim_risk: "SLSA L3" on GitHub-hosted runners trusts GitHub, its runner images, and Sigstore; it proves where/how built, not that source or deps are benign (xz source was legitimately built).
underclaim_risk: Provenance + reproducible double-build removes the "build host compromise" class cheaply and is machine-verifiable by consumers.
specifics: Workflow: build job (no id-token) uploads artifact; separate reusable `attest.yml` called with `permissions: {id-token: write, attestations: write, contents: read}`; all actions pinned by 40-char SHA; protected `release` environment with required reviewer; verification step in a clean container: `gh attestation verify ./srv -R <org>/<repo> --signer-workflow <org>/<repo>/.github/workflows/attest.yml`. Pass: verify exit 0 and double-build hashes equal. slsa-github-generator last push 2026-08-07 (604 stars).

title: Update/signing stack: Sigstore Rekor v2, TUF (tough), threshold signing (FROST, threshold ML-DSA)
summary: Sigstore Rekor v2 GA Oct 2025 (tile-based, Tessera; hashedrekord+dsse only; no SET so needs RFC3161 timestamp authority; cosign >=3.0.1/2.6.0, DSSE-to-Rekor-v2 needs cosign >=3.1.0; public-good default may still be v1). TUF client: tough 0.24.0 (2026-07-10, awslabs, 233 stars; spec follows TUF 1.0.0 with exceptions: delegated roles/TAP3/TAP4 historically unsupported); two high GHSAs published 2026-05-05 fixed in tough>=0.22.0/tuftool 0.15.0: GHSA-8m7c-8m39-rv4x (delegated-role signature threshold bypass via duplicated signature, CVE-2026-6966) and GHSA-4v58-8p28-2rq3 (missing delegated metadata validation, CVE-2026-6967) -- a TUF library with a threshold-bypass bug is itself a TCB item. Threshold signing: RFC 9591 FROST (June 2024, Informational) with Ed25519 ciphersuite yields standard RFC 8032 signatures; Zcash Foundation frost-core/frost-ed25519 3.0.0 (2026-04-23); Least Authority audit of the Zcash FROST demo completed 2025-04-29 (not of the library release). PQ threshold is research-stage: Quorus (ePrint 2025/1163, USENIX Sec 2026, honest majority, 37-136 rounds), ePrint 2026/013 (<=1MB/party up to 6 parties, Go impl), arXiv 2601.20917 (unreviewed), Pebble (Jul 2026); no production Rust crate found. Practical threshold today = TUF root/targets thresholds (k-of-n independent keys) rather than FROST.
overclaim_risk: CVE ids 2026-6966/6967 came from a search snippet; GHSA ids confirmed via GitHub API but not CVE mapping. FROST != PQ; ML-DSA threshold schemes unaudited.
underclaim_risk: k-of-n TUF thresholds with offline hardware keys already give multi-party release approval without novel crypto.
specifics: L5: update channel = TUF repo (tuftool 0.15+ for authoring, tough >= 0.24.0 pinned in client; cargo-vet audit of tough required because of 2026 bugs); root threshold 3-of-5, targets threshold 2-of-3, snapshot/timestamp online keys; clients reject rollback. Test: own negative tests replicating GHSA-8m7c duplicate-signature case against the client (must reject). Decision: FROST only if a single aggregated Ed25519 signature is a hard requirement; PQ signing of releases = ML-DSA/SLH-DSA single-key with multiple independent signatures (sibling PQC track).

title: DST harness spec for an async Rust HTTP server (tokio + hyper + turmoil, sans-IO core)
summary: Layered design from evidence: (1) protocol/WAL/authz core as sans-IO state machines (fn handle(Event)->Vec<Action>; no async, no clock reads) as in rustls/quinn-proto and Polar Signals (receive(msg)/tick(now), one PRNG, failure injection once at the message bus); (2) async shell on tokio current_thread with paused clock, hyper 1.12 server on turmoil::net::TcpListener (turmoil examples/axum is a working precedent), clients as turmoil hosts; (3) Storage trait with in-sim implementation modelling torn/lost/misdirected writes and fsync semantics (turmoil-fs 0.1.0 is 5 days old, 14 downloads = prototype only); (4) all entropy via injected Rng (rand_chacha 0.10 seeded from DST_SEED) and all time via Clock trait; (5) mad-turmoil 0.2.1 in sim binary only for dependency leakage + fastrand::seed; (6) TLS: do NOT run aws-lc/ring inside the sim (raw getrandom syscall bypasses libc interposition; see as.dst-entropy-leak); test TLS via rustls sans-IO state machine tests + fuzz + BoGo, and run the sim over plaintext HTTP/1.1+h2 or a deterministic test CryptoProvider; (7) Oracles: linearizability of the idempotent-write/WAL API (porcupine-rs 0.3.0 or Go Porcupine as S2 does), failed request => no state mutation, idempotency key => at-most-once side effect, bounded memory per connection/stream, framing consistency (no desync), authz decision monotonicity.
overclaim_risk: No head-to-head evidence that this layering beats madsim/bach/Antithesis for a server; S2 used turmoil+mad-turmoil, Polar Signals chose state machines, TigerBeetle built bespoke; 17 notable bugs at S2 is a vendor count.
underclaim_risk: Both S2 and Polar Signals report real data-loss/duplication/deadlock bugs found; effort to make dependencies deterministic was "substantial" but unquantified.
specifics: Pins: tokio 1.54.1 (features test-util, rt), turmoil 0.7.2, mad-turmoil 0.2.1 (cfg(sim) only), rand 0.9/rand_chacha 0.10, porcupine-rs 0.3.0. Faults per seed (sampled from the seed): packet drop/reorder/partition/latency via turmoil, host crash+restart (state loss of unsynced storage), half-open sockets, slow-loris clients, request floods (rapid-reset, CONTINUATION, empty DATA analogues), clock skew via Clock trait, disk faults (torn write, fsync error, bit rot, lost write). clippy.toml disallowed-methods [Instant::now, SystemTime::now, thread::spawn, rand::thread_rng] and disallowed-types [HashMap, HashSet] (verified to fire) in all sim-reachable crates. CI gates: (G1) determinism meta-test: run seed S twice, hash full TRACE log, must match (S2 does this and it caught nondeterminism); (G2) entropy canary: `strace -f -e trace=getrandom,clock_gettime,gettimeofday -o t.log ./sim --seed S` must show 0 calls after init (or seccomp-kill filter); (G3) PR: >=200 seeds x 60 simulated seconds, 0 oracle failures; nightly: >=20,000 seeds (32-core box parallel single-threaded processes); every failing seed committed as regression test with git commit pinned (TigerBeetle: seed+commit reproduces). (G4) sim-vs-kernel conformance suite for each Storage/Net shim run against real kernel (turmoil real-uring-conformance feature is the pattern). (G5) fault-coverage assertions: each fault class must fire >=1 time in the first 1000 seeds (TigerBeetle: assert positive+negative cases occur).

title: Miri, loom, shuttle, sanitizers: coverage limits and CI use
summary: Miri (rust-lang/miri, 6.7k stars, daily): single-threaded interpreter, no networking, little platform API/FFI support, unsupported syscalls error, cannot find bugs only in other thread schedules unless run with many seeds (default 64 in many-seeds mode), and a clean run is not a soundness proof. title: Embedded durable store selection for single-node/household tier
summary: No Rust-native embedded store has a clean 2026 crash-consistency record. SQLite (C, WAL) has the longest field record but a 14-year latent WAL-reset corruption bug (fixed 2026-03/04). redb and fjall each fixed power-loss/crash-recovery bugs in the last 3 months. LMDB is mature in C but its Rust binding heed had UB-at-open until 0.23 (2026-10-22). sled never left alpha. Choice should be made by running our own fault-injection harness, not by README claims; default candidate = SQLite WAL synchronous=FULL on >=3.53.0 / 3.51.3 / 3.50.7 / 3.44.6; alternative = redb with Durability::Immediate and check_integrity on open.
specifics: Alternatives enumerated independently: SQLite, redb 4.4.0, fjall 3.1.12, heed 0.23.0/LMDB 1.0.2, sled 1.0.0-alpha.124, rocksdb crate 0.25.0, libmdbx, turso 0.9.0-pre.1, canopydb 0.2.5, own WAL (TigerBeetle-style).
overclaim_risk: Over: treating a recent clean release as evidence of absence of bugs; every store here has had silent-loss bugs fixed in 2026.

title: SQLite WAL: version, bug history, fault model
summary: Latest 3.54.1 (2026-10-16). WAL-reset corruption bug present 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09); fixed 3.51.3 (2026-03-13), mainline 3.53.0 (2026-04-09), backports 3.44.6 and 3.50.7; triggers only with >=2 connections writing/checkpointing at the same instant; SQLite says rate is at or below SSD-malfunction rate. WAL + synchronous=NORMAL: commits NOT durable on power loss (only checkpoint syncs); docs say run with FULL. 3.50.2 fixed frames-without-checksum after savepoint rollback with spill. 3.51.0 hardened against close() breaking POSIX locks. howtocorrupt: no fork() of connections, no unlink/rename of db or -wal, lying drives, NFS, copying live db. Single-process single-writer-connection architecture avoids the WAL-reset trigger entirely.
specifics: L5: pin libsqlite3-sys bundling >=3.53.0 (or 3.51.3+); PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; synchronous=FULL; one writer connection per process; wal_autocheckpoint tuned; no forking after open; backup only via VACUUM INTO / sqlite3_rsync / backup API.
overclaim_risk: Over: 'SQLite is proven' - the WAL-reset bug lived 16 years undetected.
underclaim_risk: Under: that bug needs concurrent writer/checkpointer connections; single-writer design is outside it.

title: Exactly-once side effects: what is and is not achievable
summary: ACHIEVABLE: (1) exactly-once EFFECT when the effect and the dedup/checkpoint record commit in one atomic transaction in one store (DBOS transaction steps: 'records the outcome atomically in the same database transaction'; transactional outbox/inbox; Kafka EOS inside Kafka). (2) effectively-once when the downstream peer enforces an idempotency key (Stripe; Golem docs: 'external exactly-once requires the peer to enforce an idempotency key'; header alone insufficient). (3) at-most-once per attempt (Temporal maximumAttempts=1; AWS StepSemantics.AtMostOncePerRetry) at cost of possible zero executions. NOT ACHIEVABLE: exactly-once execution of an arbitrary external side effect across a crash between effect and journal write (Two-Generals class); every engine's recovery re-runs interrupted steps: Temporal (at-least-once activities, race when attempt exceeds StartToClose timeout), Conductor, Cloudflare Workflows (steps 'may be retried'), AWS durable SDK ('neither guarantees the step runs exactly once'), DBOS (interrupted step retried). Netherite paper: exactly-once not generally implementable, proposes causally-consistent commit. Also concurrent-resume race: k resumers => effect fires k times (arXiv 2608.03836, 36/40 cells).
specifics: L5 invariant (SPEC_INVARIANTS): for each external effect class declare one of {tx-colocated, peer-idempotent(key), at-most-once, human-reconcile}; no effect class may be declared 'exactly-once' without tx-colocation or peer dedup proof. Effects not colocated must carry deterministic idempotency key generated INSIDE the journaled step.
overclaim_risk: Over: vendor pages say 'exactly once' (Restate).
underclaim_risk: Under: tx-colocated exactly-once is real and cheap when the app DB is the effect store.

verify.note: 2608.03836 covers LangGraph/CrewAI/pydantic-graph only; general claim rests on vendor docs + Netherite impossibility.

title: 'Failed request => no state mutation': DB txn vs CoW write buffer vs saga
summary: Evidence ranking: (a) single DB transaction per request is the strongest existence proof - PostgREST runs every request in one transaction (default READ COMMITTED), SET LOCAL ROLE + set_config(...,true), COMMIT unless error, all queries prepared. Limits that break the invariant even there: sequences/nextval and setval are never rolled back (PG docs), side effects outside DB, ambiguous commit when connection drops after COMMIT sent, 40001 serialization failures require whole-txn retry (docs), Jepsen found Postgres 12.3 serializable G2-item anomaly present since 2011 (fixed Aug 2020) and RDS Multi-AZ 17.4 Long Fork on reader endpoint. (b) In-process per-request CoW buffer (stage writes, flush at success) gives atomicity only for the buffered store and only if flush itself is atomic - reduces to (a) at flush; no independent verification evidence found for a CoW-buffer-as-isolation design; Cloudflare output gates are the closest production analogue (response held until storage ack). (c) Sagas: compensations are semantic not physical, need durable execution to guarantee they run (CIDR26); suitable for cross-system effects, not for local state. Conclusion: invariant must be stated as 'no committed DB mutation unless the request reached its commit point; external effects only after commit via outbox or idempotent key', with sequences and ambiguous commit explicitly carved out.
specifics: L5 invariant text: INV-NOMUT: for every request r with outcome != Committed, the set of durable user-visible rows changed by r is empty, modulo {sequence values, advisory-lock side effects, pg_stat counters}; proven by construction (one txn per request, no autonomous commits, no COMMIT from handler code), tested by DST with injected failure at every await point.
overclaim_risk: Over: 'atomic request' claims ignoring ambiguous commit and sequences.
underclaim_risk: Under: single-txn-per-request is cheap and well-evidenced.

title: PostgreSQL docs: RLS caveat list

title: Transaction-pooling session-state leak class (SET ROLE / GUC / advisory locks)
summary: In transaction pooling the backend is reassigned between clients; session state set by one principal can reach the next. PgBouncer docs: SET/RESET 'Never' safe in transaction mode, server_reset_query (DISCARD ALL) not run in transaction pooling, track_extra_parameters default tracks session_authorization, search_path (PG18+) etc but not role. PgDog open issues: #1850 (2026-10-18) search_path/statement_timeout/TimeZone leak to next client via SET inside txn, multi-statement queries, set_config(), DO blocks; #1341 (2026-08-11, v0.1.52) SET ROLE leaks current_user because RESET ALL skips GUC_NO_RESET_ALL role (fix PR #1444 adds RESET SESSION AUTHORIZATION); #1407 session advisory locks leak. Supavisor PR #1113 (merged 2026-07-22) adds opt-in txn_mode_leak_action detecting session SET, set_config(..,false), DISCARD, session advisory locks, LISTEN, WITH HOLD cursors, temp tables, LOAD (default 'ignore'). Safe pattern: all identity via SET LOCAL / set_config(...,true) inside an explicit txn; ban session-level state at the protocol/AST layer; or avoid third-party pooler by owning the pool in the gateway.
specifics: L5 invariant INV-NOSESSIONSTATE: after any statement the backend's session-level GUC/role/lock/prepared state equals the pool baseline; enforced by (1) rejecting non-LOCAL SET, set_config(,,false), DISCARD, LISTEN, advisory session locks, WITH HOLD, temp tables, LOAD at AST level, (2) DISCARD ALL + RESET SESSION AUTHORIZATION on check-in, (3) canary test: client A sets everything, client B asserts baseline.

Architecture implication: independent layers - (a) gateway statement allowlist by fingerprint, parameters only; (b) per-principal role with column grants and default-deny, no ambient owner; (c) RLS as defense-in-depth keyed on SET LOCAL txn-scoped claims; (d) no shared mutable pooler session state; (e) pin and canary every PG minor with RLS regression corpus. title: L5: storage crash/fault-injection harness acceptance gate
summary: Spec: wrap storage in a recording VFS/fs shim (ALICE-style) that logs write/fsync/rename/ftruncate; enumerate persistence-state prefixes and reorderings between fsyncs; add bit-granularity corruption (flip each bit of header/padding, misdirected-write chunk swaps, stale-block restores as in Jepsen TigerBeetle); inject fsync EIO and require abort-not-retry (fsyncgate); after each state run recovery + invariant checker: (i) every acked commit present, (ii) multi-table batch atomic, (iii) get==range, (iv) no panic on any corrupt byte (Result::Err Corrupted only), (v) idempotent recovery (crash during recovery). Gate: 0 violations over N=10^5 crash states per candidate store in CI nightly; candidate stores that fail are excluded. title: L5: DB gate invariants and CI gates
summary: INV-ALLOW: gateway forwards only Parse messages whose pg_query fingerprint is in the committed allowlist; Bind parameters only; no Query ('simple') messages, no COPY, no multi-statement. INV-NOSESSIONSTATE (see txn-pooling node). INV-ROLE: each request runs as SET LOCAL ROLE <tenant-class role> inside BEGIN..COMMIT, authenticator NOINHERIT, no BYPASSRLS, no table-owner connections, FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on all tenant tables, column-level GRANTs only, REVOKE ALL on schema public from PUBLIC. INV-NOMUT as above. INV-IDEMP: idempotency record (tenant,key,fingerprint,status,response) inserted in the same txn as the effect. CI: (1) RLS regression corpus + tenant-isolation property test (two tenants, random statements, assert no cross-read/write) on pinned PG minor and on PG beta; (2) pooler canary leak test; (3) allowlist drift check; (4) cargo-deny/audit for sqlx, pg_query, pgwire, tokio-postgres RustSec; (5) PG minor version >= 18.6/17.11. DESIGN IMPLICATION: every per-request resource (interned strings, header tables, integer width) needs a per-connection budget enforced BEFORE allocation; isolation unit must own its memory (per-handler arena/instance), not share a global table. title: PHP's crash immunity is process-level recycling plus watchdogs, not a language property; no public crash-isolation measurements exist
summary: Share-nothing = every request rebuilds state, shared data pushed to DB/cache tier (Lerdorf: 'scale horizontally infinitely'). FPM implements robustness operationally: pm.max_requests (respawn to work around leaks in 3rd-party libs), request_terminate_timeout (kill worker), emergency_restart_threshold (restart FPM if N children SIGSEGV/SIGBUS in interval), all default OFF. PHP internals 2020 thread: isolation seen as robustness feature; Swoole/RoadRunner give up isolation for speed. I found no quantified public data on crash blast radius or per-request bootstrap cost.
specifics: php.net FPM config manual; externals.io/message/108253 (2020); tideways blog; talks.php.net share-nothing slides. DESIGN IMPLICATION: define 'PHP miracle' as four testable invariants: (I1) handler fault (panic/abort/OOM/infinite loop) affects only that request, (I2) no cross-request memory residue, (I3) per-request CPU/mem/time hard cap, (I4) crash-loop damping (threshold analog of emergency_restart). Acceptance gate: chaos test injecting each fault class at 5% of requests while 95% concurrent healthy requests keep p99 within 1.2x baseline.
overclaim_risk: Claiming PHP is 'crash-immune': a SEGV in a shared extension kills the worker and its in-flight request; FPM needs a threshold knob because it can crash-loop.
underclaim_risk: Ignoring that real hosting (WordPress, Facebook-era) ran at huge scale on this model; density came from simplicity, not proofs.

title: CGI->FastCGI->AOLserver: the cost of isolation was per-request state setup; the fix was pooling OUTSIDE the isolation boundary
summary: FastCGI (Open Market, spec v1.0 1996-04-29, Mark R. Brown) removed per-request process creation by persistent processes. AOLserver (NaviSoft->AOL 1995, open-sourced 1999) combined multithreading, embedded Tcl and pooled persistent DB connections (~100x vs CGI per Wikipedia only), at the price of in-process shared fate; NaviServer fork 2005 still active. Pattern: isolation cheap if expensive state (DB conns, compiled code) lives in a trusted pool and handlers receive references.
specifics: FastCGI spec/whitepaper (whitepaper URL 404 on Apple mirror; spec at mit.edu mirror). DESIGN IMPLICATION: connection pools, TLS sessions, prepared-statement caches live in a broker; handlers get capability handles; falsifiable bench: per-request instantiate+DB-handle-acquire overhead < 100us p50 at >=10k rps on one core, else isolation boundary is mis-placed.
overclaim_risk: 100x figure is a single Wikipedia sentence.
underclaim_risk: AOLserver's architecture (threads+pools+script) became the template for most app servers.

title: Ur/Web statically rules out injection and gives automatic CSRF signing, but explicitly does NOT guarantee authorization correctness
summary: Per the manual's Security Model (FFI unused, checkable from .urp): no SQLi/XSS (code is AST, not strings), automatic CSRF via signed cookies when a handler reads cookies and has side effects, locked-down stdlib (no filesystem). Explicit non-guarantees: any endpoint can be called with any args/cookies; CSRF signature not handler-specific; FFI voids warranty. POPL'15 (not PLDI): compiler SML ~55,000 LOC, server runtime ~5,000 LOC C, client ~1,500 LOC JS.
specifics: Chlipala POPL'15 DOI 10.1145/2676726.2677004; urweb doc/manual.tex 'Security Model'. DESIGN IMPLICATION: type-level removal of injection classes is a solved, cheap result (typed SQL + typed HTML AST); AEGIS must get it in its handler SDK (parameterized-query-only DB API, HTML as AST) and must add an authz layer Ur/Web lacks; invariant test: no API path exists that accepts a raw SQL/HTML string without a named unsafe_ escape hatch, enforced by grep-able lint + cargo-geiger-style budget.
overclaim_risk: Saying Ur/Web 'prevents CSRF' without the cookie/signature caveat.
underclaim_risk: Underrating: BazQux/Bitparking ran years with no reported classic web vulns (self-reported by developer, grade C).

title: Ur/Web stayed niche: bus factor 1, no release since 2020-02-09, TechEmpower strength unrevalidatable

title: Hails (OSDI'12): IFC web framework with measured 1.7x throughput loss vs Jetty and poor policy-API ergonomics; repos dormant since 2016
summary: Haskell/LIO, model policies (trusted) vs view-controllers (untrusted). httperf, 100 closed-loop conns, 2x Xeon E5620, GbE: Pong 47,577 r/s vs Jetty 82,275 (1.7x fewer), +28% vs Apache+PHP, 47x Sinatra; Table 30%/23% below Jetty/PHP, 6x Sinatra; no response pipelining blamed. Experience: 4 developers; policy implementation API 'difficult to learn'; one blog app leaked unpublished posts via policy bug; mass-assignment bugs became non-vulnerabilities thanks to policy; privilege delegation largely avoided.
specifics: scslab/hails 52 stars last push 2016-09; scslab/lio 3 stars 2016-07. DESIGN IMPLICATION: security policy must be a small declarative artifact owned by trusted code, with analysis (SMT) over policies; test: policy-DSL conformance suite where an agent-written handler with deliberately wrong code cannot read rows outside policy (differential: same handler with/without policy returns different rows only where policy denies).
overclaim_risk: Hardware is 2012; do not quote 1.7x as current.
underclaim_risk: Hails numbers (PHP comparable) show IFC overhead was not what killed it.

title: LWeb (POPL'19) and Storm (OSDI'21) fixed Hails' blockers: 2-21% overhead, then zero runtime cost, TCB <1% of app code
summary: LWeb: LIO+Yesod, noninterference mechanized in Liquid Haskell, 2-21% runtime overhead vs manual checks, BIBIFI site with 40 tables, TCB ~1% of app (21% incl. LWeb). Storm: refinement-typed security ORM over LIO, trusted code <1%, no runtime cost, 1 type annotation per 19 LOC (1/29 non-trivial), verification seconds per controller on i7-8550U laptop, 9 ported policy case studies, deployed Disco (107 users, peak 55, 2020). Limitation: controllers confined to restricted RIO monad; exceptions hard.
specifics: Both Haskell/Liquid Haskell, research-grade, no production adoption found. DESIGN IMPLICATION: statically-checked authz/IFC on DB access is feasible at ~5% annotation tax; the annotation tax is exactly what coding agents are good at; falsifiable pilot: have an agent write 10 handlers against a Rust refinement/typestate DB-gate API; success = >=90% compile+pass policy tests within 5 iterations, and 0 policy-violating handlers compile.
overclaim_risk: Storm 'no run-time cost' is relative to the unchecked LIO baseline on case studies, not a system benchmark.
underclaim_risk: These papers show perf was never the real blocker; ecosystem and language choice were.

title: Joe-E/Waterken: capability-safe Java subset worked (13K SLOC Joe-E + 4K Java server), but library taming was the admitted weakest link
summary: Joe-E verifier (Eclipse plugin) statically checks capability discipline; Waterken server uses it to prove persistence consistency (Immutable-marked Transaction/return types prevent vat escape). Authors call taming the Java stdlib 'time-consuming and difficult... a substantial weakness'; DarpaBrowser review found taming mistakes in E's database. Requires capability-training for developers. Repo davidwagner/joe-e 4 stars, last push 2015-06.
specifics: NDSS 2010 (Mettler, Wagner, Close); Mettler thesis EECS-2012-244. DESIGN IMPLICATION (Rust analog): the stdlib is the taming problem. Enforce no-ambient-authority by (a) deny std::fs/net/process/env via clippy disallowed-methods + a workspace lint, (b) route all effects through cap-std style Dir/Pool handles, where code must call ambient_authority() explicitly (cap-std docs note it is not a sandbox against unsafe). CI gate: cargo-deny/grep fails build if any handler crate references std::{fs,net,process,env} or declares unsafe.
overclaim_risk: Waterken's persistence property is about one server, not a deployed ecosystem.
underclaim_risk: Rust's ownership gives much of Joe-E's 'no static mutable state' for free; the residual is unsafe + stdlib ambient APIs.

title: Web-key/YURL capability URLs: the bearer-URL design leaks (Referer, http, third-party scripts); W3C TAG could only issue non-normative good practices
summary: Tyler Close's httpsy://, YURLs and web-key put authority in the URL (hash of root key inside, so key replacement keeps URLs valid). W3C TAG 'Good Practices for Capability URLs' (Tennison, non-normative Finding, 2014) was motivated by leaked doc-sharing URLs and lists leak routes; Referrer-Policy helps but 'is not enough'. TAG did not dispute but never endorsed web-key.
specifics: DESIGN IMPLICATION: never carry bearer authority in URLs or anywhere it can be logged; use sender-constrained tokens (DPoP/mTLS/HTTP message signatures) for capabilities, plus Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and log redaction. Test: crawl all responses/logs from an e2e run for any token-shaped string in URL, Referer or access log (must be zero).
overclaim_risk: Not evidence that capabilities-as-tokens fail; only that URL transport is a bad bearer channel.
underclaim_risk: Macaroon/Biscuit-style attenuable tokens are the survivor of the idea.

title: Caja (rewriting sanitizer) was archived after repeated bypasses; the freeze-the-realm descendant (SES/Hardened JS/Endo) survived in production
summary: Caja advisories: 2009 DOM-wrapper full-page escape and iframe schema hole, 2013 ES5 freezing and javascript: URI flaws, 2018-era XSS and Unicode-escape bypass found by a bounty hunter while Google Sites ran an unpatched Caja; Google archived repo 2021-01-31 citing unmaintained against modern research and known vulns (repo last push 2020-12-02). SES 'starts where Caja left off': lockdown() freezes intrinsics, compartments, harden(); third-party assessment June 2021 and July 2021 bug hunt found no criticals; Agoric kernel model formally verified sound. TC39: SES Stage 1 'very stale' (2022), recast as Hardened JavaScript; ShadowRealm orthogonal; Compartments cut to module loader API; Moddable XS implements. Endo: 1069 stars, Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-10-15; users Agoric, MetaMask (LavaMoat, Snaps run iframe+LavaMoat+SES layers). Documented non-guarantees: no CPU/memory/availability isolation (one agent), stack observable on JSC, covert channels via host endowments, TCB includes engine.
specifics: DESIGN IMPLICATION: in-process language-level capability sandboxes give authority control but NOT resource control; for untrusted/agent code AEGIS needs a resource-metered boundary (process/microVM/wasm with fuel) UNDER any language-level capability layer. Falsifiable: guest running `while(1)` or allocating unboundedly must be killed within X ms without affecting neighbours; SES alone fails this test by documented design.
overclaim_risk: TC39 thread is July 2022; status may have moved. No quantified lockdown overhead found.
underclaim_risk: Underclaim: Hardened JS is the only 'ocap web' lineage with real production users (MetaMask).

title: Why type-safe/capability/IFC web systems failed to be adopted: blocker matrix and which blockers coding agents remove
summary: Blockers across Ur/Web, Hails, Swift, Joe-E, Caja, E/Waterken, Fable: (1) annotation/proof burden - agents remove (Storm 1/19 LOC; vericoding 82% Dafny); (2) runtime overhead - mostly not the killer (LWeb 2-21%, Storm 0, Hails 1.7x vs Jetty); (3) library/stdlib taming and ecosystem (Joe-E, Ur/Web FFI, SES jQuery incompat) - NOT removed, agents can write but not make third-party code capability-safe; (4) bus factor/maintenance (Ur/Web 86% one author; Hails dormant 2016; Caja archived) - NOT removed; (5) confusing whole-program errors - partly removed (agents read errors); (6) policy-spec fidelity (Hails leaked posts) - NOT removed; (7) availability/resource control absent (SES) - needs OS/VM layer.
specifics: DESIGN IMPLICATION: invest agent effort in (1),(2),(5); invest human/process effort in (3),(4),(6); falsifiable roadmap check: every dependency on the critical path has >=2 maintainers org-level, a vendored reproducible build, and an executable-spec oracle.
overclaim_risk: Synthesis across papers; causality of 'died' is inferred, no authors' retrospective found for most.
underclaim_risk: May understate that these systems simply never had a funded product team.

title: Wasmtime Oct 2026 critical sandbox-escape batch (Cranelift bit-pack + aarch64 br_table + async callback BOF)
summary: Three critical wasmtime advisories in 3 weeks: GHSA-897f-g5gm-fmxm (CVE-2026-115889, Cranelift SSA index bit-packing overflows silently in RELEASE builds; a very large/crafted Wasm function => type confusion => sandbox escape on ANY arch with DEFAULT config; fixed v43, backport 36.0.19), GHSA-mghf-wjfp-p5xm (CVE-2026-115893, aarch64 br_table wrong jump, 36.0.19/48.0.7/49.0.4), GHSA-32h6-97mm-8q3c (CVE-2026-115384, component async-lifted callback result count unvalidated => native stack BOF, >=39.0.0, fixed 48.0.4/49.0.2). ~37 wasmtime GHSAs 2026-08-25..10-20, dominated by component-model-async/WASIp3/wasi-http panics, fuel-accounting bypasses (exponential fuel amplification via call_ref/catch, poll_oneoff skips fuel), GC heap corruption, uncapped handle tables, wasi fs sandbox escape via symlink rename. wasmtime 50.0.0 released 2026-10-20.
specifics: L5: pin wasmtime >=49.0.4 or >=50.0.0 (or 36.0.19 LTS line); gate: cargo-deny advisory check + reject any wasmtime < patched; enforce Config max_wasm_stack, module/function size caps (limit function body bytes) and use Cranelift only (Winch had its own critical Apr 2026); never rely on Wasm as sole boundary for third-party/agent code: wrap in seccomp+Landlock+separate process (or microVM). Disable component-model-async/WASIp3 unless needed (most Oct advisories are there).
overclaim_risk: Counting advisories overstates risk if most are panics/DoS in preview features; only 3 are sandbox-escape class.
underclaim_risk: Dismissing as 'patched' misses that class (compiler miscompile) recurs; a verified compiler backend is absent; 36.0.19 shows it was latent for years across LTS.

title: MCP spec revision 2026-07-28: stateless protocol, no sessions, MRTR, DCR deprecated
summary: Primary changelog verified. Removes Mcp-Session-Id and initialize handshake (SEP-2567, SEP-2575); every request carries protocolVersion/clientCapabilities in _meta; server/discover; subscriptions/listen replaces GET stream and resources/subscribe; SSE resumability (Last-Event-ID) removed - broken stream loses in-flight request, client re-issues with new request id; MRTR (SEP-2322) replaces server-initiated roots/sampling/elicitation with InputRequiredResult retry; tasks moved to extension (SEP-2663); Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name headers (SEP-2243); ttlMs/cacheScope on list results (SEP-2549); RFC 9207 iss validation MUST (SEP-2468); RFC 7591 DCR deprecated for Client ID Metadata Documents; Roots/Sampling/Logging deprecated with 12-month policy (SEP-2577/2596); JSON Schema 2020-12 for tool schemas (SEP-2106); OTel traceparent in _meta. Previous rev 2025-11-25.
specifics: L5: target 2026-07-28 as primary MCP projection; server holds NO per-connection protocol state => idempotency/WAL keyed by explicit server-minted handles + request ids; request routing by Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name headers enables L7 policy before body parse; implement server/discover; keep 2025-11-25 compat shim behind adapter. rmcp (rust-sdk) at 3.7.0 on 2026-10-22 - verify it tracks this revision before depending.
overclaim_risk: Secondary articles claim 'MCP 2.0'; the spec itself is a dated revision, not a major version.
underclaim_risk: Statelessness removes whole session-hijack class but pushes state into tool handles (new confused-deputy surface).

verify.note: "iss MUST" overstated (MUST validate only when present).

title: PortSwigger HTTP Terminator (2026-09-28): autonomous AI desync research factory
summary: Kettle's pipeline (ideation/evaluation/weaponization/cascade) ran on c7i.2xlarge, 2000 threads, 30k sites <1 req/s/domain; novel techniques: HTTP/1.0+TE:gzip CL.0, multipart/byteranges Content-Type as CL.0 trigger (>200 sites incl. a US bank), dual matching Content-Length treated as 0, dangling-byte RQP, 'Shared-Parser Confusion' (request input reaching response-only parsing features); Apache Traffic Server zero-day CVE-2026-63078; F5 BIG-IP, Beyond Trust, NetScaler cases. Recommends: avoid upstream HTTP/1.1, method allow-lists, no bodies on GET/HEAD/OPTIONS. To be open-sourced. Model attribution unspecific (OpenAI+Anthropic).

overclaim_risk: Vendor-run offensive research; counts of affected sites not independently audited.
underclaim_risk: Evidence that novelty can be machine-generated at ~1 rps scale - time-to-exploit for parser differentials is collapsing.

title: RFC 10024 (PQ/T hybrid key agreement for TLS 1.3, Proposed Standard, ~Aug 2026); RFC 9954; RFC 9846 TLS 1.3 bis
summary: Verified on rfc-editor.org: RFC 10024 defines X25519MLKEM768 (0x11EC, IANA Recommended Y), SecP256r1MLKEM768 (0x11EB, N), SecP384r1MLKEM1024 (0x11ED, N); authors PQShield/AWS/Cloudflare/Waterloo. title: FIPS mode reality: X25519MLKEM768 not negotiable in RHEL FIPS mode; P-256/P-384 hybrids are
summary: Red Hat RHEL-94614/RHEL-95239: only secp256r1MLKEM768 and secp384r1MLKEM1024 work in FIPS mode. OpenSSL docs: X25519MLKEM768 orders shared-secret parts opposite to SP 800-227 convention. FIPS profile should default to SecP256r1MLKEM768 (0x11EB).
overclaim_risk: Verifier-sourced; single verification pass.
